All these punctures, if they can be ascribed to something else such as a butcher or wolf having clenched (the animal) - we attribute it to them. But if there isn't something to ascribe it to, if there's a doubt if it was punctured while alive or not, we poke a puncture next to it and compare them. And even if they don't look alike, if they palpated the suspected puncture they should palpate also the puncture that they made to compare it with; if they look alike after palpating it's kosher. But we only compare in the Keres a
and not in the heart or spleen or Korkeban.

Rema: See above in #36 regarding the custom whenever we are unable to ascribe it to something after it's been shechted. Even though it's treifot that can be checked, if they didn't check it or they're unable to check it, behold it's like safek treifah and we forbid it. We don't consider it an allowed shechita except in something where we could say the defect happened after shechita so that it hasn't been excluded from its chazakah of viable.

Any body part that we said that if it's pierced any mount it's treif, so if it's missing entirely it's treif, whether it's missing by illness or by action or it was created missing it. The same if it was created with two of that body part, it's treif, because any extra is considered like it's missing (except for the spleen in which case if it's missing it's kosher, but a puncture in is somekh (support?) is treif) (Tur). And everything that we said that if it's created missing it then it's treif, all the more so if it's missing by action. And all that we said that if it's removed it's treif, it's the same rule if it's created missing it, but there are some who rule this kosher.

(o.o.) (And if it's a big loss it's you can rely on those who rule it kosher).

Any body part that invalidates it if it's punctured or missing or removed, if it's decomposed it invalidates it too.

Rema: But for us who are not expert - whenever the flesh is altered to a fault, it should be considered as a puncture there (H"M and Mord').
